title: Dedicated staged rollouts: autoscaling guardrails + minimum headroom enforcement
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description: Problem: Dedicated staged rollouts shift traffic between model/runtime/config variants while staying within a reserved GPU pool. In partial stages (e.g., 5%/25%), we can end up in a bad state where the new variant consumes more GPU/latency than expected and the pool has insufficient headroom to absorb retries/queueing, violating Dedicated SLOs. We also saw in dogfood that stage advancement + autoscaling can briefly “chase” the new load and saturate before metrics/gates catch up. This PR adds a hard guardrail: do not allow stage application/advancement if it would violate a minimum headroom policy for the pool. Approach: 1) Add a headroom check in the rollout stage transition path (control plane -> capacity policy evaluation), 2) Integrate with existing Dedicated autoscaling guardrails (min spare replicas / GPU headroom), 3) Add explicit config toggles (per-tenant + per-pool) to enable/disable and tune thresholds, and 4) Emit metrics + structured logs so SRE can see when rollouts are being blocked by headroom vs. gates. Behavior: On stage transition request (manual approval or automatic advancement), the control plane computes the target traffic weight for the candidate stage and queries the pool capacity snapshot. If projected headroom < threshold, we block applying the stage and set rollout status to HOLD with reason=INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM (operator can retry after capacity changes). We intentionally fail safe (HOLD) rather than proceeding. If guardrail is disabled, behavior is unchanged. Config: - rollout.headroom_guardrail.enabled (default: true for internal dogfood pools, false for external until beta allowlist) - rollout.headroom_guardrail.min_headroom_pct (default: 0.15) - rollout.headroom_guardrail.min_spare_replicas (default: 1) - rollout.headroom_guardrail.mode: block | warn (warn emits metrics/logs but does not block; intended for beta ramp-up) Observability: - redwood_dedicated_rollout_headroom_check_total{result="pass|block|warn",pool_id_hash,tenant_id_hash} - redwood_dedicated_rollout_headroom_block_total{reason="min_headroom_pct|min_spare_replicas|snapshot_stale"} - redwood_dedicated_pool_headroom_ratio (gauge, sampled, low-cardinality dims) - Structured log event: rollout_headroom_check (includes rollout_plan_id, stage_id, target_weight, computed_headroom_pct, required_headroom_pct, spare_replicas, snapshot_age_ms). Notes: This is not a replacement for gate evaluation (latency/5xx/queue depth). It is an additional precondition that avoids obviously unsafe transitions when the pool is already near saturation or capacity telemetry is stale. Related: ENG-5130. This PR is meant to work with the routing stage weights work (PR #28479) and the evaluator fail-safe behavior (PR #28572).
commits: dedicated/autoscaling: add headroom projection helper for staged rollouts
control-plane: block stage apply when headroom policy violated (HOLD reason)
config: per-tenant + per-pool toggles for rollout headroom guardrail
telemetry: emit rollout headroom check metrics + structured logs
tests: unit tests for projection math + snapshot stale handling
review_conversation: Irene Choi: Can we clarify what snapshot we’re using for projected headroom? If it’s older than a minute, blocking seems correct, but we should make that threshold explicit and surfaced in the HOLD reason.

Keiko Yamamoto: Good call. Added snapshot_age_ms to the structured log + a hard threshold (30s) for block mode; warn mode just emits. HOLD reason now includes snapshot_stale as a distinct reason string.
Mina Haddad: Does this run before or after we update routing weights? I want to avoid partial application where routing flips but stage state remains HOLD.

Keiko Yamamoto: It runs before routing updates; stage transition handler now short-circuits before writing the stage version or pushing the routing policy bundle. Added a test for “no routing write on blocked transition”.

Sean Gallagher: Metric naming: please avoid pool_id dimension. Hash ok, but make sure it’s sampled. Also add an alertable counter for blocks so oncall can correlate ‘rollout stuck’ with headroom enforcement.

Keiko Yamamoto: Updated. pool_id_hash only, plus sampling at 1/20 for high-volume pools; block counter is unsampled + low cardinality. Follow-up dashboard work is in ENG-5131 but this gives the primitives.

Jordan Lee: Projection math: are we assuming linear scaling with weight? That’s ok as a first approximation, but let’s document it. Also ensure the guardrail is per-pool and cannot be overridden by tenant policy unless explicitly allowed.

Keiko Yamamoto: Added docs inline + comments: linear assumption over recent utilization window; if pool is already near saturation we’ll block regardless. Override is operator-only; tenant-scoped config cannot disable block mode when operator sets it.
Vanessa Ortiz: Can we add a manual escape hatch for incidents? E.g., operator can proceed despite block, but it must be auditable.

Keiko Yamamoto: I didn’t add bypass in this PR because it ties into approvals/audit events (PR #28558). For now, operator can temporarily set mode=warn on the pool config; that change is already audited via existing config change logs. I noted this in the PR and added a TODO for an explicit ‘bypass with audit event’ follow-up.
release_notes: Dedicated staged rollouts now enforce autoscaling minimum headroom guardrails before applying/advancing stages. Rollouts will pause (HOLD) when pool capacity headroom is insufficient or capacity metrics are stale. Adds config toggles (enabled/mode/min_headroom_pct/min_spare_replicas) and emits rollout headroom check metrics/logs for oncall debugging.
notes: Default remains disabled for external Dedicated tenants pending beta allowlist; internal dogfood pools can enable warn mode immediately. If you see HOLD reason=INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM, check pool snapshot freshness + autoscaler headroom dashboard, then either add capacity/headroom or retry stage advancement once stabilized.
